keywords.markdown:
Defines an immutable `local` binding. It is a syntax error to try to change the value of this binding.

```luwu
const x = 2
x += 1 -- syntax error

const function foo()
    do_something()
end
```
A `do` expression runs its block and evaluates to the value its `give` gives.

Create loop statements to iterate over containers (or a set number of times).

```luwu
-- iterate over an array
const cats: { string } = { "Taz", "Nyla", "Nanuk", "Crazy", "Mr. Purrsalot" }
for index, cat in cats do
    print(cat)
end

-- iterate over a map
const animals: { [string]: Animal } = get_animals()
for animal_name, animal in animals do
    print(`name: {animal_name}`)
end

-- iterate 10 times
for i = 1, 10 do
    print(i)
end

-- iterate through an array backwards
for i = #cats, 1, -1 do
    print(i, cat)
end
```
Separates the clauses of an `if` condition; the branch runs only when every clause passes.
Exits the enclosing `do` expression with this value.

Choose between two expressions based on a condition; `if` *expressions* evaluate to a value rather than branching control flow.

```luwu
const name = if typeof(value) == "string" then value else tostring(value)

const level =
    if score > 100 then
        "Expert"
    elseif score > 50 then
        "Intermediate"
    else
        "Beginner"
```

Unlike `if` statements, `if` expressions contain exactly one expression per branch, evaluate to at least one value, require an `else` branch, and do not terminate with `end`.

refinements.markdown:
```luwu
function name_of(thing: unknown): string?
```

----------
The name of anything that has one.

```luwu
function class.implements(o: unknown, t: trait): boolean
```  
*Refines* `o` into an object of `t`

----------
Returns `true` if `o` is an object of a class that implements trait `t`, whether the class lists
`t` after `implements` or gets it through another trait that `needs` it.

If `o` is not an object, returns `false`. Raises a runtime error if `t` is a class rather than a trait
(use `class.isinstance` for classes).

In the type system, this refines `o` to the trait:

```luwu
local function describe(value: unknown): string?
    if class.implements(value, Named) then
        return value.name
    end
    return nil
end
```

```luwu
local thing: Named
```
*This object implements* [`Named`](refinements.luwu#L1)

----------
The name of anything that has one.


----------

```luwu

trait Named
    expect name: string
end
```

```luwu
literal<string>
```

----------
A literal of `string`: the value as written, like `"-f"` or `true`, rather than any `string`. Literals exist for strings and booleans.

On a parameter, callers have to pass a literal, and the function body sees `string`; on a local, the local has the literal's own type. Write `literal<S>` with a generic `S` to infer `S` as the literal (`sym("foo")` gives `Symbol<"foo">`).

Passed to a type function (`Validate<literal<string>>`), the type function checks each argument as written and can reject it with `types.error(message)`. A type alias can name either form for use in parameters.

traits.markdown:
```luwu
trait Health
    expect max_health: number
    health: number
    function damage<Self>(self, amount: number): Self
end
```
*Jump to* [`Health`](traits.luwu#L2)

----------
Something that takes damage and can run out of health.

Marks a member of a trait that every implementing class must declare itself.

```luwu
trait Tool
    expect private model: Model
    expect public function equipped?(self) -- `?`: classes may leave this one out
    expect function __init(self, props: Props) -- a constructor taking these arguments
end
```

```luwu
public function damage<Self>(self: Self, amount: number): Self
```

----------
Takes `amount` off [Health](traits.luwu#L2%2C1), never going below zero, like [math.max](https://luau.org/library#math-library) would.

```luwu

    const name: string
    max_health: number
    health: number  -- from Health
    function damage(self, amount: number): Player  -- from Health
end
```
